themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 17 this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1411% jump (z-score: 12.51)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Ridgewood/Glendale that emerged THIS WEEK and warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 17 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (1411% spike, z-score: 12.51)
Statistically significant outlier with highest z-score in dataset
Timing coincides with potential loss of enforcement or organized posting campaign
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD/Sanitation enforcement: Are crews understaffed? Did enforcement pause?
Canvass neighborhoods to map where postings are clustered—suggest targeted enforcement response
Contact community board: Has graffiti/posting been flagged as ongoing complaint in budget requests?

themes_detail.label: Park Disturbances & Unleashed Dogs
themes_detail.summary: This week, noise complaints from parks jumped 7100% (9 complaints vs. 0.1 average, z-score: 26.84), and unleashed dog complaints surged 900% last week (5 vs. 0.5 average). Combined with park rule violations up 700%, this suggests a sudden loss of park supervision or weekend event impact that is NEW and concentrated.
evidence: Noise - Park: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (7100% spike, z-score: 26.84—highest severity)
Unleashed Dog: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.5 average (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Violation of Park Rules: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community board budget requests include park reconstruction/upgrades—suggests long-standing maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Visit major parks (Ridgewood Park, etc.) to observe conditions and dog compliance firsthand
Interview Parks Dept: Was there a staffing cut, special event, or removal of enforcement detail?
Talk to residents: Are noise complaints tied to specific times/days or specific groups?

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped 357% THIS WEEK (12 complaints vs. 2.6 weekly average, z-score: 7.69), suggesting a storm event, disease outbreak, or lack of routine tree maintenance that requires rapid Parks Dept response.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 12 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 7.69)
Timing suggests acute event (storm, disease) rather than chronic issue
Community board repeatedly requests park reconstruction/upgrades—indicates systemic maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Check weather records: Was there a storm or unusual weather event THIS WEEK in the district?
Contact Parks NYC: Are they investigating disease (e.g., emerald ash borer, oak wilt)? What trees are affected?
Canvass specific blocks to identify which species/neighborhoods are hardest hit—localizes story impact

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged 700% last week (8 vs. 1.0 weekly average, z-score: 5.29) and vendor enforcement complaints jumped 700% (6 vs. 0.8 average, z-score: 4.82), signaling either a new homeless/informal economy concentration or enforcement response that emerged LAST WEEK.
evidence: Encampment: 8 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.29)
Vendor Enforcement: 6 complaints last week vs. 0.8 average (700% spike, z-score: 4.82)
Parallel spikes suggest interconnected issue (informal economy + housing insecurity) or coordinated enforcement
reporting_angles: Locate encampments and interview unhoused residents: Why the sudden spike? What services exist?
Interview street vendors: Are enforcement sweeps new? Are they targeting specific blocks or product types?
Contact NYPD/Sanitation: Was there a targeted enforcement action or policy change LAST WEEK?
Human interest: Profile an affected resident or vendor—explain how district policies impact their daily lives

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints hit 3 cases 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average—a 380% spike (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting a possible foodborne illness outbreak or contaminated food source that warrants public health follow-up.
evidence: Food Poisoning: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 4.91)
Timing suggests acute outbreak rather than chronic food safety issue
No recent local news coverage of outbreak—possible undercovered public health risk
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Dept: Was there an outbreak investigation 2 weeks ago? Any restaurants flagged?
Review restaurant inspection records from that week—match 311 complaints to specific establishments
Interview affected residents: What did they eat? Where? Do symptoms match confirmed pathogen?
Public health angle: Are food vendors/restaurants in the district receiving adequate inspections?
